title: Is the ship the destination, or the *transport*?
subtitle: Answer that honestly and half your shortlist disappears.

text: Sea days are either the point or the penalty.
sub: There is no middle position. Every ship is designed for one answer, and the itinerary quietly tells you which one it chose.

left.label: Destination
items: Sea days you look forward to

right.label: Transport
items: Cabin as a place to sleep

points.label: Sea days, counted
points.value: Two or more in a week means the ship is expected to hold you. It had better be able to.

points.label: An overnight in port
points.value: A rare and telling inclusion. It says the town matters more than the dining rooms.

points.label: Late departures
points.value: Anything after six turns dinner ashore from an argument into an actual evening.

points.label: Tender calls in July
points.value: The most fragile day on any summer itinerary, and the least often flagged to you.

items.head: A grand ship, a port sprint
items.body: You paid for the public rooms and then spent every day ashore. The ship was wasted on you.

items.head: A spartan ship, a crossing
items.body: Six sea days with nowhere good to sit is a long time in which to regret a fare.

items.head: Eight calls in ten nights
items.body: It reads beautifully on the page and it is quietly exhausting by the fourth morning.

text: I'd rather sell you fewer ports on the right ship.
sub: The route is what people book. The ship is what they remember. When those two disagree, the ship wins — every single time.

title: Send this to the person you'd sail with
body: Ask them the question on the first slide. If your answers differ, send me both and I'll find the compromise.
